claim: measured (counts from the private per-segment tables of workers 108, 111 and 115, re-joined by the segment index; nothing re-read from AWS)
taking_the_51: the segments of class FLOW_TIMING_CONVENTION_DOLLARS_TIE in worker 108's membership table (51 of 90); each of the 51 lands in exactly one cell of the cross-tabulation below and in exactly one group (cells sum 51, groups sum 51; uncovered by subtraction: 0).
what_is_settled_for_all_51: The four dollar items (beginning value, ending value, net additions, net gains) tie in 51 of 51 (DB-b-135).
The set of flow days in the custodian's rows equals the served set of flow days in 51 of 51 (DB-b-138); the rows fix the DAY of every flow.

With each transaction id counted once, the custodian's day flow equals the served day flow to half a cent on 234 of 235 flow days (DB-b-142), in 50 of 51 segments on every day; the one day left is a day on which the ledger carries an administrative expense row (action Other Fee) that the method does not count as a flow (line 706 of the producer).
Counted once per id, the custodian's net additions tie in 89 of 90 segments (DB-b-144); this cell uses that only as context.
what_is_not_settled_for_all_51: The time of day at which the custodian credits a flow (in the opening value, the closing value or between) is not shown by any record this project can read. Under START timing the return closes within 0.35 pp for 50 of 51, under MID for 48 of 51, under END for 0 of 51 (DB-b-135, DB-b-138); that is a fit to the custodian's returns, not a read of the custodian's rows. Round 68 refuted FLOW_TIMING where the event-date sets agree; they agree in 51 of 51, so for these 51 the only thing the refutation leaves open is the intraday placement, and the refutation is not reinterpreted here.

flow_reproduces.note_on_the_one: The one segment reproduces on every day if the single Other Fee expense row is left out of the day (51 of 51 segments reproduce on that reading), which is what the producer's rule says for an administrative expense. The shared code table's class for that row is being read by cell DB-b-146, whose result was pending when this record was made; this record does not assume it. The segment is held in its own group (group 1) until that result is in.

crosstab.axes: flow reproduces on every day with ids counted once (yes/no) x DB-b-138 outcome x the timing under which the return closes within 0.35 pp
crosstab.outcome_meaning: O1 = every readable flow day enters the value on its posting day, rows fix the date, intraday not shown (25); O2 = ledger dollars did not reproduce the served flow when summed without the id (14), now explained by the id repetition; O3 = no determinable flow in the daily value series (12)
crosstab.one_timing_fits_all: No single timing closes all 51: START leaves 1 segment outside tolerance and MID leaves 3.

groups.meaning: The flow's amount is settled on every day except one, on which the custodian's rows carry an administrative expense (Other Fee) that the method does not count as a flow. If that row is rightly outside the flow the segment's flow reproduces to the cent on every day and the segment then has the same open question as group 4; until the row's class is read, its flow is not claimed settled.
groups.what_would_close_it: The shared code table's class for that one Other Fee row, read by cell DB-b-146 (result pending when this was written). This project can obtain it: it is a read of a table already in its reach. Once it agrees with the producer's rule the segment moves to group 4 for its timing question; a disagreement is a row against the table.

groups.meaning: Amount and day of every flow are settled; the restated returns under START, MID and END lie within 0.35 pp of one another, so the choice of timing moves the return by less than the tolerance. END alone still falls outside the tolerance against the custodian's figure.
groups.what_would_close_it: A ruling by the CTO that a fit within 0.35 pp under one stated timing is accepted as the classing. This project can obtain it (it is an internal ruling); no custodian record is needed because the timing does not move the return beyond the tolerance.

groups.meaning: Amount and day of every flow are settled; the return closes under only one of the two timings: START only in 3 segments, MID only in 1. The fit that separates START from MID points in different directions for different segments, so no one stated timing covers them.
groups.what_would_close_it: A custodian statement of the convention it applies to the time of day of a flow, saying whether it is one rule for every account or varies. This project cannot obtain it from any record it can read; whether the custodian publishes such a statement or an intraday series is NOT_ESTABLISHED here, and asking the custodian is not an act this cell takes. Without it, the only other route is a CTO ruling that a fit under whichever one stated timing closes a segment is the classing (4 of 4 close under exactly one of the two), which would accept a convention that differs between segments.

groups.meaning: Amount and day of every flow are settled; START and MID both close the return within 0.35 pp and END does not, and at least one flow day is large enough against the account's own daily moves, with a next day present, to show in the daily value series that it enters on its posting day (or, for one segment, is ambiguous there). The fit separates END from START or MID and cannot separate START from MID; the rows and the value series show the day, not the time of day.
groups.what_would_close_it: A custodian statement of the convention it applies to the time of day of a flow (opening, closing or between), which would make START or MID a fact and not a fit. This project cannot obtain it from the records it can read; whether the custodian offers it is NOT_ESTABLISHED here. The alternative is the CTO ruling in group 2, applied to both timings (START and MID both fit).

groups.meaning: Amount and day of every flow are settled; START and MID both close the return and END does not; no flow day in the segment is both large enough against the account's own daily moves and followed by a next day, so even the daily value series shows no entry day. The only test left is the fit to the custodian's return.
groups.what_would_close_it: A custodian intraday or daily-opening value series for the segment's flow days, or a custodian statement of its convention. The daily end-of-day series this project reads cannot test an intraday position for these segments at all. This project cannot obtain either from any record it can read; whether the custodian provides one is NOT_ESTABLISHED here. Failing that, nothing obtainable from the project's own records would close the group beyond the CTO ruling in group 2.

tieout_state.composition: classed = 154 (DB-b-129) + 31 accrual-class (DB-b-135); contested = the 51; unclassed = 8. No segment is moved by this record.

proposal: PROPOSAL, NOT A RULING: the tie-out should keep the 51 CONTESTED and show them beside the 8 UNCLASSED with one stated reason instead of the retired flow-timing wording -- amount and day of every flow are settled (the flow reproduces to the cent with ids counted once in 50 of 51 segments, the 51st pending the class of one expense row; the four dollar items tie in 51 of 51), and what is open is only the time of day the custodian credits a flow, which START or MID fit within 0.35 pp and END does not, and which no record this project can read shows; the CTO rules whether a fit within the tolerance under a stated timing is accepted as the classing.
not_established: The time of day at which the custodian credits a flow: no record read shows it.
Whether the custodian publishes a statement of its flow-timing convention or an intraday series: not looked for in this cell and not read by it.
The shared code table's class for the one Other Fee row: pending in cell DB-b-146.

Group 5 and group 4 are separated by the daily-series readability rule of DB-b-138 (flow at least 5 times the account's own median non-flow daily move and at least 1 percent of the prior value, with a next day present); a different readability rule would move segments between them, not out of the 51.
derivation_note: Groups: first the segment whose flow does not reproduce on every day (1); then segments whose START, MID and END restated returns lie within 0.35 pp of one another (3); then segments closing under exactly one of START or MID (4); then the remaining 43 split by whether the daily value series has a readable flow day (32 yes, 11 no), the readability rule of DB-b-138 re-applied with the ledger now reproducing (its outcome O2 took 14 segments before the entry-day test could run; re-applied, 12 of those have every readable flow entering on its posting day and 2 are ambiguous). DB-b-138's own outcomes stand as filed in the cross-tabulation.
